title: Stipulated remedies: editorial notes and questions
summary: Read the surrounding notes and questions alongside the principal cases. The complete assigned pages are preserved here.
notes:
Figgie International, Inc. v. Destileria Serralles, Inc.: Figgie connects interpretation and remedies: first identify the remedy the parties’ agreement contains, including trade usage, and only then decide whether that remedy remains enforceable. It demonstrates why a case needs to appear in more than one topic index.

Dave Gustafson & Co. v. State: This decision supplies a successful example of advance damages estimation. Compare its size-and-duration formula with the saved-cost problem in Lake River and the gross-receipts problem in Wasserman’s.

Lake River Corp. v. Carborundum Co.: Lake River makes the relationship between revenue, saved expenses, and lost profit concrete. It also illustrates how a federal court separates its policy preferences from its responsibility to apply state contract law.

Wasserman’s Inc. v. Township of Middletown: Wasserman’s shows why concern about a formula does not always justify deciding its validity on summary judgment. The lease’s economic value and the nature of the loss matter alongside sales figures.

Swiss Federal Supreme Court: contractual penalty decision of September 24, 2024: This comparison prevents the word “penalty” from silently carrying the same legal consequence across jurisdictions.
